name: The Stockade
summary: The Stockade holds dangerous prisoners beneath Stormwind's canal district near the Mage Quarter. Built as a high-security prison for cutthroats, political insurgents, and captured enemies of state, it has fallen into violent anarchy. Warden Thelwater is forced back to the entrance, seeking help to crush the riot before it reaches the capital.

sections.title: A Prison Under Siege
sections.body: Beneath Stormwind's canals, the Stockade has become a war zone. When the regular army marched to distant fronts, the understaffed prison relied on inexperienced youths, including fourteen-year-old recruits, to keep order. They failed. The inmates launched a bloody, coordinated rebellion, tore their wool blankets into gang scarves, and cut down the remaining guards. Warden Thelwater barely holds the entrance, while convicts control the cells, hallways, and holding blocks.

sections.title: Nobles and Assassins
sections.body: The riot exposed Stormwind's political dealings. Outside territories had grown frustrated with the House of Nobles halting executions for its own leverage. Redridge guard Berton wanted the captured orc Targorr the Dread executed for atrocities, but the nobles froze his sentence. Darkshire councilman Millstipe saw grave robber Dextren Ward spared the gallows despite desecrating graves for the necromancer Morbent Fel. The dwarves of Dun Modr also demanded the death of Dark Iron saboteur Kam Deepfury. With the Stockade in chaos, local authorities quietly hired adventurers to carry out the executions the capital's courts refused to enforce.

sections.title: The Mastermind and the Rioters
sections.body: Bazil Thredd, a cunning felon tied to the Defias Brotherhood, orchestrated the uprising from his cell. Bruegal Ironknuckle, a dangerous dwarven brawler, is among the rioters. He is one of several hardened convicts adventurers may meet while helping Thelwater reclaim the prison.

faq.q: Why is the Stockade in open rebellion?
faq.answer: The Defias Brotherhood orchestrated a prison-wide riot while the facility was severely understaffed. With the Stormwind Army deployed to distant battlefronts, teenage volunteers guarded hardened killers. The convicts ambushed the staff, seized weapons, and drove Warden Thelwater out of the cellblocks.

faq.q: Who is running the uprising inside?
faq.answer: Bazil Thredd, an influential Defias felon incarcerated in the eastern cellblock, masterminded the revolt. Other dangerous prisoners include Bruegal Ironknuckle, Hamhock, and Kam Deepfury.

faq.q: Why are prisoners like Targorr and Dextren Ward still alive?
faq.answer: Both were condemned to death, but corrupt politicians in the House of Nobles placed bureaucratic holds on their executions to use the prisoners as political leverage. This interference outraged allies in Lakeshire and Darkshire, who sent adventurers to eliminate them during the chaos.

faq.q: What does defeating Bruegal Ironknuckle mean for the prison?
faq.answer: Bruegal Ironknuckle is a dangerous dwarven brawler among the rioters. Defeating him removes one threat while adventurers work to put down the uprising.

faq.q: Why are there Dark Iron dwarves and orcs inside a human jail?
faq.answer: The Stockade is a maximum-security holding pen for high-value prisoners of war. Targorr the Dread led Blackrock orc attacks in Redridge, while Kam Deepfury sabotaged the Wetlands for the Dark Iron clan. Both were captured and transferred to the capital.

faq.q: Can Horde players enter the Stockade?
faq.answer: Yes, but entering is exceptionally hazardous. The dungeon portal sits inside Stormwind City near the Mage Quarter canals. Horde infiltrators must sneak past the city guards and the capital's defenders to reach it.

angles.text: The rebellion threatens Stormwind's internal security and the heart of the capital. Putting it down preserves that security and honors off-the-books bounties for Redridge, Duskwood, and Ironforge.
Kam Deepfury's presence in Stormwind's cells affronts Dun Modr. The Kingdom of Ironforge demands his head to avenge dwarven lives lost in the Wetlands.
The prison's intricate web of locked iron cells and Defias connections offers unique lockpicking practice and insight into Bazil Thredd's underworld syndicate.
The prison lies on the canal edge of the Mage Quarter, where physical brawlers are vulnerable to slowing spells. The ogre mage Hamhock can unleash Chain Lightning.
